items.note: "Flambeado" on Spanish sushi menus means torched with a flame (aburi style); rendered as "flame-seared" rather than "flambéed", which in English implies alcohol. Used consistently for all "flambeado" items.
"Langostino" rendered as "king prawn" throughout, to keep it distinct from "gamba" ("prawn").

"Solomillo" = tenderloin/fillet; the carta does not say which animal (probably beef, and a guest photo shows a seared beef nigiri), so it is kept neutral. "Fillet" alone would read as fish on a nigiri list.

items.note: The carta says "envuelto de" (wrapped in), but a futomaki has the nori outside and guest photos show the fish and surimi inside the roll. Elsewhere on this menu "wrapped in X" means X is the outer layer, so "filled with" is used here.

"Shake" is the Japanese word for salmon and is already rendered by "Salmon"; not kept in brackets, where English readers would take it for a milkshake.

items.note: "Rollitos" on Spanish Asian menus are spring rolls (rollitos de primavera), and guest photos show fried spring rolls. On a sushi menu a bare "rolls" would read as maki. Same for 902 and 903.
"Empanadillas" = small fried turnovers/pasties; "curry puffs" is the usual English name for fried pastries with a curry filling.

"Pan frito" here is fried Chinese buns (guest photos show round golden fried buns, i.e. mantou). "Fried buns" rather than "fried bread", which in British English means a fried slice from a full breakfast. "Mantou" is not added, since the carta does not say it.
